tools.name: extract
tools.description: Extract a public URL and return its content as plain text, markdown or HTML using Desearch. Markdown keeps headings, lists and tables. Text is the page's main content; set full_page for every section, such as opening hours or fee tables. A js_required error means the page needs js: true; blocked means the site refused or showed a bot check. Preferred over web-crawl for new integrations. API docs: https://www.desearch.ai/docs/api-reference/get-web-extract

format.description: Content format to return: 'text' (default), 'markdown' (headings, lists, tables and code) or 'html'.

js.description: Render JavaScript before reading the page.

wait.description: Post-load wait in milliseconds when JavaScript rendering is enabled.

full_page.description: Only with format 'text': return all visible text of the page (every section, table and notice) instead of only its main content.

tools.name: web-crawl
tools.description: Crawl a public URL and return its content as plain text or HTML on the legacy Desearch /web/crawl route. The SDK marks webCrawl deprecated in favor of extract; this tool stays for parity with that route. Prefer extract for new integrations. API docs: https://www.desearch.ai/docs/guide/apis/extract-api

format.description: Content format to return: 'text' (default), 'markdown' (headings, lists, tables and code) or 'html'.

js.description: Render JavaScript before reading the page.

wait.description: Post-load wait in milliseconds when JavaScript rendering is enabled.

full_page.description: Only with format 'text': return all visible text of the page (every section, table and notice) instead of only its main content.

tools.name: people-search
tools.description: Start a paid job billed to the user's Desearch balance: find people on X, YouTube, LinkedIn, or TikTok who match a plain-language description. Returns a task_id at once, with the task's status and reserved_cost_usd. Cost: the call reserves count times the platform's per-person price at the time of the call (reserved_cost_usd; prices at https://desearch.ai/pricing). When the search ends you pay only for the people it delivered (final_cost_usd; a per-search minimum applies when it finds anyone; a search that finds no one is free) and the rest of the reservation is returned. Data: each person comes back with a fit score, why they matched, their audience, and only the contacts and links they list publicly. Desearch reads public data only. X: public posts and public profile fields (bio, followers, website, location). YouTube: public channel pages (About section, subscribers, country, links) and the creator's own website for publicly listed contact details. LinkedIn: public posts and public profiles (headline, company, location, followers, about). TikTok: public videos and public profiles (bio, followers, likes, latest videos, a public email listed in the bio). People found stay readable for 30 days after the search ends. The search runs in the background, usually for 1 to 5 minutes: poll people-search-status with the task_id to read progress and the people found so far, and use people-search-pause, people-search-resume, or people-search-cancel to pause, resume, or cancel it. Do not start the same search twice; send idempotency_key so a retry returns the first task instead of charging again. Filters depend on the platform. x: min_followers, max_followers, verified_only, countries, keywords, exclude_keywords. youtube: min_subscribers, max_subscribers, countries, require_contact, keywords, exclude_keywords. linkedin: min_followers, max_followers, countries, keywords, exclude_keywords. tiktok: min_followers, max_followers, require_contact, keywords, exclude_keywords.

platform.description: Where to look: 'x' (X profiles), 'youtube' (YouTube creators), 'linkedin' (LinkedIn members), or 'tiktok' (TikTok creators).

query.description: Who you are looking for, in plain language, example: 'Skincare creators who review sunscreen'.

count.description: How many qualified people to find (5-200, API default 25). The search reserves this many and bills only the people it delivers.

min_score.description: Only return people with at least this fit score (0-100).

exclude.description: Handles to leave out, for example people you already contacted.

idempotency_key.description: Any unique string for this search, for example a UUID. Sending the same key again returns the first task and is not charged again.

metadata.description: Your own labels for this search, example: {"campaign": "q4-outbound"}. Up to 10 keys; keys are 1-40 characters of a-z, 0-9, '_', '.', '-'; values are strings of up to 200 characters. Returned on the task; filter people-search-tasks by it. The search does not use it.

min_followers.description: Minimum follower count. x, linkedin, tiktok.

max_followers.description: Maximum follower count. x, linkedin, tiktok.

verified_only.description: Only verified or X Premium accounts. x only.

require_contact.description: Only creators with a public email (tiktok: in the bio; youtube: an email or contact link). youtube, tiktok.

countries.description: Countries to prefer, example: ['US', 'GB']. x, youtube, linkedin.

keywords.description: Words that should appear in their posts, videos, or bio. All platforms.

exclude_keywords.description: Leave out people who mention these words. All platforms.

tools.name: people-search-status
tools.description: Status, progress, and cost of one People Search task, plus a page of the people found so far: name, handle, url, platform, audience, location, fit score, why they matched, contacts, and links. Free: it reads a search you already started and runs no new search. Cost fields are reserved_cost_usd and, once the search ended, final_cost_usd. People come from public profiles and posts on the search's platform, with only the contacts they list publicly. People arrive while the search runs: pass the returned next_cursor as cursor on the next call to get only the people found since then. When done is true and has_more is false you have everyone the search found. An ended task has completion_reason (why it stopped), coverage_limited: true when a budget stopped it before count (more people may match), and warnings such as partial_enrichment (some profiles could not be read, so those people were scored on the search hit; they show enrichment: failed). Each person has fully_verified (every criterion confirmed by their own profile or posts) and unverified_criteria (criteria that are unknown or not met, or a disqualifier that applies). These are information only: the person still qualified.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous people-search-status call. Omit to start from the first person.

include_people.description: Set false to read only the status, progress, and cost.

tools.name: people-search-pause
tools.description: Pause a People Search task and return its updated status. Free: it charges and refunds nothing. A queued search pauses at once; a running one finishes its current batch first (status pausing, then paused). Pausing loses no data: the people found so far stay readable with people-search-status, and the search keeps its progress. Billing does not change: the reservation made when the search started stays reserved while paused and is settled only when the search ends. Undo it with people-search-resume, which continues from where the search stopped with no new charge. Limit: a search paused for more than 7 days is cancelled by the API and can no longer be resumed; you then pay only for the people already delivered, the rest of the reservation is returned, and the people found stay readable for 30 days.

tools.name: people-search-resume
tools.description: Resume a paused People Search task and return its updated status. Free. The search continues from where it stopped, keeping the people already found, with no new charge: the cost already spent is carried forward and the original reservation still covers it. Works only on a paused search, within 7 days of pausing; a search in any other state, including one the API cancelled after 7 days paused, returns 409. Poll people-search-status for the new people.

tools.name: people-search-cancel
tools.description: Cancel a People Search task. Free. The search stops for good; you pay only for the people it already delivered and the rest of the reservation is returned. People found so far stay readable for 30 days. This cannot be undone.

tools.name: people-search-tasks
tools.description: Your People Search tasks, newest first, with status, counts, cost, why each ended search stopped (completion_reason, coverage_limited), and the metadata labels set on people-search. Free; it lists your own tasks, not the people they found (read those with people-search-status or people-profiles). Use it to find a task_id (filter by metadata to find the searches of one campaign), or to see which searches are still queued, running, or paused: a new search is refused while too many are active.

platform.description: Only tasks on this platform: 'x', 'youtube', 'linkedin', or 'tiktok'.

status.description: Only tasks in these statuses, example: ['running', 'paused'].

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Keep the same metadata filter when you page.

metadata.description: Only tasks whose metadata has all of these key/value pairs (exact match, up to 3), example: {"campaign": "q4-outbound"}.

tools.name: people-profiles
tools.description: Everyone your own People Searches found on one platform, one entry per person: their best-scoring result (name, handle, url, audience, location, fit score, why they matched, public contacts, and links) and the search that found them (found_by). Free: it reads only people your earlier searches found, runs no new search, and queries no outside source. That data came from public profiles and posts, with only the contacts each person lists publicly. Search by name, handle, bio, or location with q, filter by contact channels (has), audience, fit score, location, or verification, and sort by score, recent, or audience. People from searches that ended more than 30 days ago are left out.

q.description: Text in the name, handle, bio, or location, example: 'skincare'.

has.description: Channels every person must have, example: ['email', 'instagram']. 'email' is a public email; the others are a link of that type.

location.description: Text in the location, example: 'united states'.

verified.description: Only verified accounts. Only X and TikTok people carry a verified flag.

tools.name: company-search
tools.description: Start a paid job billed to the user's Desearch balance: find companies on the web that match a plain-language description, and collect each one's public contact data. Returns a task_id at once, with the task's status and reserved_cost_usd. Cost: the call reserves count companies at the Company Search per-company price at the time of the call (reserved_cost_usd; prices at https://desearch.ai/pricing). When the task ends you pay only for the companies it delivered (final_cost_usd; a minimum of 2 when it delivers any; a task that delivers none is free) and the rest of the reservation is returned. A company left out by min_score or require is not billed. Each company has a fit score (0-100) and why it matched, plus fully_verified and unverified_criteria (what its own pages do and do not confirm). Data: Desearch reads public data only: each company's own website (its homepage and its contact, about, team, and imprint pages), public web search results, and public LinkedIn profiles of its leaders. Each company comes back with its location, public emails, phones, and social profiles, and its leaders (roles) with their title, LinkedIn profile, and emails. Every contact keeps the page it came from (source_url). Leader emails can be inferred from the company's address pattern (source: inferred, with a confidence), and every email is checked (verification: valid, invalid, risky, or unknown). Companies stay readable for 30 days after the task ends. The task runs in the background: poll company-search-status with the task_id to read progress and the companies delivered so far. Each company is delivered first with enrichment status partial, and the later stages (contact pages, leaders, inferred emails, email checks) fill it in until it is complete. Use company-search-pause, company-search-resume, or company-search-cancel to pause, resume, or cancel it. Do not start the same task twice; send idempotency_key so a retry returns the first task instead of charging again. To read companies you already know by domain, use company-enrich instead.

query.description: The companies you are looking for, in plain language: what they do, where, how far along. Example: 'Series A fintech startups in Berlin building payment infrastructure'.

count.description: How many companies to deliver (5-200, API default 25). The task reserves this many and bills only the companies it delivers.

min_score.description: Only deliver companies with at least this fit score (0-100).

exclude.description: Companies to leave out, as domains or URLs, for example ones you already contacted (up to 1000). Each is reduced to its host without www.

countries.description: Where the companies should be: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes or country names, example: ['DE', 'Austria'] (up to 20). Scoring treats them as a location criterion. Sent as filters.countries.

require.description: Only deliver companies that have all of these: 'email', 'phone', 'linkedin' (the company's LinkedIn page), 'leader' (one of roles), 'leader_email' (a leader with an email). A company is delivered once the stage that can show them has run (email, phone, linkedin: the contact pages; leader: the leaders; leader_email: the email checks); one that does not have them is not delivered and not billed. Sent as filters.require.

roles.description: The leaders to look for: any of 'ceo', 'founder', 'cto', 'cfo', 'coo', 'cmo', 'president', 'owner', 'managing_director' (API default ['ceo', 'founder', 'cto', 'cfo']). A managing director (Geschäftsführer) counts as 'ceo' when 'ceo' is asked for.

infer_emails.description: Guess leaders' emails from the company's address pattern (for example first.last), learned from the addresses found on its site (API default true). Inferred emails say source: inferred and carry a confidence: high when the pattern was learned from this company's own addresses, low for a common pattern.

verify_emails.description: Check every email: syntax, mail server (MX) and, for inferred ones, a web search (API default true). Each email then has a verification: valid, invalid, risky, or unknown. Set false to finish sooner without it.

idempotency_key.description: Any unique string for this task, for example a UUID. Sending the same key again returns the first task and is not charged again.

metadata.description: Your own labels for this task, example: {"campaign": "q4-outbound"}. Up to 10 keys; keys are 1-40 characters of a-z, 0-9, '_', '.', '-'; values are strings of up to 200 characters. Returned on the task; filter company-search-tasks by it. The task does not use it.

tools.name: company-enrich
tools.description: Start a paid job billed to the user's Desearch balance: collect public contact data for companies you already know, by domain. Send 1-200 domains or URLs; each is reduced to its host without www., lowercased, and deduplicated, and the task reads every one. Returns a task_id at once, with the task's status and reserved_cost_usd. You get one company per domain with the same fields as company-search but no fit score (score is null). The task's count is the number of domains left after deduplication. Cost: the call reserves one company per domain sent at the Company Enrich per-company price at the time of the call (reserved_cost_usd; prices at https://desearch.ai/pricing). When the task ends you pay only for the companies it delivered (final_cost_usd; a minimum of 1; a task that delivers none is free) and the rest of the reservation, including duplicate domains, is returned. Data: Desearch reads public data only: each company's own website (its homepage and its contact, about, team, and imprint pages), public web search results, and public LinkedIn profiles of its leaders. Each company comes back with its location, public emails, phones, and social profiles, and its leaders (roles) with their title, LinkedIn profile, and emails. Every contact keeps the page it came from (source_url). Leader emails can be inferred from the company's address pattern (source: inferred, with a confidence), and every email is checked (verification: valid, invalid, risky, or unknown). Companies stay readable for 30 days after the task ends. The task runs in the background: poll company-search-status with the task_id to read progress and the companies delivered so far. Each company is delivered first with enrichment status partial, and the later stages (contact pages, leaders, inferred emails, email checks) fill it in until it is complete. Use company-search-pause, company-search-resume, or company-search-cancel to pause, resume, or cancel it. Do not start the same task twice; send idempotency_key so a retry returns the first task instead of charging again. To find companies from a description, use company-search instead.

domains.description: 1-200 company domains or URLs, example: ['acme.com', 'https://www.beta.io/about']. Each is reduced to its host without www. and lowercased; duplicates are removed.

roles.description: The leaders to look for: any of 'ceo', 'founder', 'cto', 'cfo', 'coo', 'cmo', 'president', 'owner', 'managing_director' (API default ['ceo', 'founder', 'cto', 'cfo']). A managing director (Geschäftsführer) counts as 'ceo' when 'ceo' is asked for.

infer_emails.description: Guess leaders' emails from the company's address pattern (for example first.last), learned from the addresses found on its site (API default true). Inferred emails say source: inferred and carry a confidence: high when the pattern was learned from this company's own addresses, low for a common pattern.

verify_emails.description: Check every email: syntax, mail server (MX) and, for inferred ones, a web search (API default true). Each email then has a verification: valid, invalid, risky, or unknown. Set false to finish sooner without it.

idempotency_key.description: Any unique string for this task, for example a UUID. Sending the same key again returns the first task and is not charged again.

metadata.description: Your own labels for this task, example: {"campaign": "q4-outbound"}. Up to 10 keys; keys are 1-40 characters of a-z, 0-9, '_', '.', '-'; values are strings of up to 200 characters. Returned on the task; filter company-search-tasks by it. The task does not use it.

tools.name: company-search-status
tools.description: Status, progress, and cost of one Company Search or Company Enrich task, plus a page of the companies delivered so far: domain, name, url, location, fit score (null for Company Enrich) and why it matched, primary_email and primary_contact, public emails, phones, and social profiles with the page each came from (source_url), leaders with their roles, title, LinkedIn profile, and emails (each with its verification status; inferred ones with source: inferred and a confidence), contact_coverage, and enrichment (status partial or complete, and each stage: profile, contacts, people, email_patterns, email_check). Free: it reads a task you already started and runs no new search. Cost fields are reserved_cost_usd and, once the task ended, final_cost_usd. The data came from each company's own website, public web search, and public LinkedIn profiles. Companies arrive while the task runs and are filled in place by the later stages: pass the returned next_cursor as cursor to get only the companies delivered since then, and call without cursor to read every company in its latest version. stage enriching means every company is delivered and only later stages of some are left. When done is true and has_more is false you have every company. An ended task has completion_reason (why it stopped; all_domains_processed for Company Enrich), coverage_limited: true when a budget stopped it before count (more companies may match), and warnings. Company Search results have fully_verified (every criterion confirmed by the company's own pages) and unverified_criteria (criteria that are unknown or not met, or a disqualifier that applies). These are information only: the company still qualified.

task_id.description: task_id returned by company-search or company-enrich, example: '5b33f3ee-168b-4780-9c8e-63a626781872'. A People Search task_id is not found here.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous company-search-status call, to get only the companies delivered since then. Omit to read from the first company, each in its latest version.

include_companies.description: Set false to read only the status, progress, and cost.

tools.name: company-search-pause
tools.description: Pause a Company Search or Company Enrich task and return its updated status. Free: it charges and refunds nothing. A queued task pauses at once; a running one finishes its current batch first (status pausing, then paused). Pausing loses no data: the companies delivered so far stay readable with company-search-status, and the task keeps its progress. Billing does not change: the reservation made when the task started stays reserved while paused and is settled only when the task ends. Undo it with company-search-resume, which continues from where the task stopped with no new charge. Limit: a task paused for more than 7 days is cancelled by the API and can no longer be resumed; you then pay only for the companies already delivered, the rest of the reservation is returned, and the companies delivered stay readable for 30 days.

task_id.description: task_id returned by company-search or company-enrich, example: '5b33f3ee-168b-4780-9c8e-63a626781872'. A People Search task_id is not found here.

tools.name: company-search-resume
tools.description: Resume a paused Company Search or Company Enrich task and return its updated status. Free. The task continues from where it stopped, keeping the companies already delivered, with no new charge. Works only on a paused task, within 7 days of pausing; a task in any other state, including one the API cancelled after 7 days paused, returns 409. Poll company-search-status for the new companies.

task_id.description: task_id returned by company-search or company-enrich, example: '5b33f3ee-168b-4780-9c8e-63a626781872'. A People Search task_id is not found here.

tools.name: company-search-cancel
tools.description: Cancel a Company Search or Company Enrich task. Free. The task stops for good; you pay only for the companies it already delivered (a task cancelled before it starts costs nothing) and the rest of the reservation is returned. Companies delivered so far stay readable for 30 days. This cannot be undone.

task_id.description: task_id returned by company-search or company-enrich, example: '5b33f3ee-168b-4780-9c8e-63a626781872'. A People Search task_id is not found here.

tools.name: company-search-tasks
tools.description: Your Company Search and Company Enrich tasks, newest first, with status, counts, cost, why each ended task stopped (completion_reason, coverage_limited), and the metadata labels set on company-search or company-enrich. Free; it lists your own tasks, not the companies they found (read those with company-search-status). People Search tasks are not listed here (see people-search-tasks). Use it to find a task_id (filter by type, status, or metadata to find the tasks of one campaign), or to see which tasks are still queued, running, or paused: a new task is refused while too many People Search and Company Search tasks are active.

type.description: Only Company Search ('search') or only Company Enrich ('enrich') tasks.

status.description: Only tasks in these statuses, example: ['running', 'paused'].

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Keep the same type, status, and metadata filters when you page.

metadata.description: Only tasks whose metadata has all of these key/value pairs (exact match, up to 3), example: {"campaign": "q4-outbound"}.

instructions: Search the public web and X with Desearch. Use search for titles and links, then fetch with a result URL to read the page. Other tools cover AI search, X posts, and page extraction. People Search finds people and creators on X, YouTube, LinkedIn, and TikTok: people-search starts a paid job billed to the user's Desearch balance, people-search-status reads progress, and people-search-pause, people-search-resume, and people-search-cancel pause, resume, or cancel it. Company Search finds companies on the web from a description and Company Enrich reads the domains you send; both collect public emails, phones, social profiles, and leaders (CEO, founders, CTO, CFO): company-search and company-enrich start paid jobs billed to the user's Desearch balance, company-search-status reads progress and the companies, and company-search-pause, company-search-resume, and company-search-cancel pause, resume, or cancel a task. Calls need a Desearch API key.
